Doctor Alexis Cowan studies light and biology. She joins Danny Jones to present what she calls the blue light agenda. Her claim is that artificial light technology is already killing people. In her account it breaks the body clocks that govern hormones, sleep, and repair. Her argument extends the show's earlier blue light episode into policy and intent.

Cowan explains the mechanisms she teaches: melanopsin, melatonin, and the metabolic cost of living under the wrong light at the wrong hours. The agenda framing, that the damage is known and allowed, is her interpretation laid over the physiology. Some of the underlying light science is solid and neglected; the intentional plot is hers to prove. Listeners get a researcher's full protocol and warning, and can adopt the practical half while judging the conspiratorial half themselves.

Comedian Kurt Metzger joins Danny Jones and goes off on the Trump cover-up, as he calls it, around Jeffrey Epstein. The episode title quotes his wildest claim: proof that Epstein is alive. Metzger is a comic known for loud, fast rants.

Metzger argues the death tale was staged and that Trump shields the truth. He fires through names, flights, and file gaps at speed. Jones tries to pin him down on what counts as proof. Listeners get a comic in full fury on the case. The library holds the talk as an archive record of the rant, not as fact.

Robert F. Kennedy Jr. joins Tucker Carlson to give news on his bid to curb the rise in autism and to open the Kennedy files. Kennedy serves as health secretary in this era of his public life. The title names both halves of his charge.

Kennedy lays out the steps he backs on food, shots, and the hunt for what drives the autism surge. He also tells where the file release stands and what still stays sealed. Carlson asks what foes block him most. Listeners hear a top health chief in his own words. The library keeps the talk as a record of his stated plans.
